# Step 8 · Python

In this step you read the brews of step 6 from Python, with the same rules as
the command line: two scripts, then a few lines typed by hand. A script can
also change values, compute and save.

Run every command from this folder, `08-python`, with the Python of the
`.venv/` above the steps, where SampleKit's Python package is installed:
`../.venv/bin/python`, or `python` once that environment is active.

## Try it

```console
$ python scripts/brew_report.py
$ python scripts/yeast_comparison.py
```

- `brew_report.py` prints what is not current, the three best brews, and
  writes the season to `season.csv`;
- `yeast_comparison.py` compares attenuation and gravity drop by yeast, and
  draws a figure the project does not declare, `yeasts.png`.

```text
smoked-porter: abv, attenuation, score

blonde-saison       44.8 ± 0.5   6.1 %
english-pale        44.7 ± 0.9   4.8 %
citra-ipa           42.7 ± 0.9   6.8 %

wrote season.csv
```

## By hand

Start `python` in this folder, and type:

```python
>>> import samplekit as sk
>>> brew = sk.Sample("brews/citra-ipa.md")       # read with its project's model
>>> brew.abv
Property(value=6.825000000000035, uncertainty=0.14510233457805027, unit='%')
>>> brew.abv.value
6.825000000000035
>>> brew["fermentation.gravity[3]"]               # any field the command line reads
1.021
>>> brews = sk.load("brews")                      # a folder: a list of samples
>>> brews.filter("style == ipa").sorted("-abv")   # as -f and -s
>>> print(brews.to_csv(columns=["name", "abv"]))  # as --csv
```

`dir(brew)` and `help(brew)` list what an object offers. A mistake raises a
standard exception with the nearest name: `brew.abvv` is an `AttributeError`.

## Changing, computing, saving

```python
>>> brew = sk.Sample("brews/dry-stout.md")
>>> brew.grain_mass.value = 4.5
>>> brew.not_current()
{'efficiency': 'outdated'}
>>> brew.compute()            # what is not current, in your own Python
>>> brew.save()               # writes the file
```

Reading never computes: a value that is not current is returned as the file
holds it, with a warning. `save()` refuses to overwrite a file that changed
since it was read. A script's saves are kept as one snapshot of the project's
history, with the script itself:

```console
$ python scripts/yeast_comparison.py
$ samplekit log
```

The script wrote a figure and saved no brew, and it is still a snapshot, since
the figure came from it; `samplekit log --script 1` prints the script as it ran.

## Why

The command line answers the questions you ask often; Python answers the one
you have not asked yet. Both read the same files by the same rules, so a
script never disagrees with a table.

- To understand: [the history](../explanations/history.md),
  and what a script leaves in it.
- To look up: [the Python package](../reference/python.md).

This is the last step. The [how-to guides](../how-to/index.md)
start your own project: [moving existing data in](../how-to/move-existing-data.md),
[a first model](../how-to/first-model.md).
